sentences.text: Daxiatitan was a massive sauropod with an estimated length of 23 to 30 meters and a neck measuring approximately 12 meters, placing it among the species with the longest necks.

This animal is distinguished from other titanosaurs by having cervical vertebrae with cranial prezygapophyseal facets that compensate caudally, such that the non-articular bone covers the cranial portions of most prezygapophyses.
The genus name honors the Daxia River, and the species name refers to Bingling Temple, both located in the region where the fossil was found.

In 2008, Daxiatitan was considered potentially the largest known dinosaur found in China, and the genus Daxiatitan and its species D. binglingi were named by You Hailu, Li Daqing, Zhou Lingqi, and Ji Qiang.

Daxiatitan is classified within the unranked family Titanosauria, and the parent group for Daxiatitan is identified as Euhelopodidae. A 2020 study suggested that Daxiatitan and Euhelopus might form a clade with mamenchisaurids.

Daxiatitan lived during the Lower Cretaceous period in Gansu, China, approximately 135 million years ago during the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous. The time range for Daxiatitan is estimated from 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
A 2020 study suggested that Daxiatitan and Euhelopus might form a clade with mamenchisaurids, though this relationship remains a hypothesis.
